spec_features.spec_quote: `give_up` is a configurable sentinel string the model may emit; hitting it sets `stop_reason="give_up"` and ends the rollout
spec_features.evidence: config.py:70 give_up_sentinel = "<<GIVE_UP>>"; harness.py SYSTEM_PROMPT instructs the model to 'emit the exact sentinel {give_up}'; in run_rollout the loop checks `if config.give_up_sentinel in (comp.text or ""): stop_reason = "give_up"; break`, which actually breaks the turn loop and sets the final stop reason.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired end-to-end: the sentinel is delivered to the subject in the system prompt, detected in assistant text, and honored as a hard stop that exits the rollout loop.

spec_features.feature_name: cache avoids re-subjecting model to same prompt
spec_features.spec_quote: never re-subjecting a model to the same adversarial prompt — is both a cost and a principle win
spec_features.evidence: cache.py JsonCache (content-addressed by sha256 of inputs); models.py ModelClient.complete builds cache_payload, computes key = make_key(...), returns the cached Completion when `cached is not None` before issuing any real API call, and stores results via self.cache.set. Identical (model, messages, seed, params) inputs are served from cache, so the subject is not re-queried.
spec_features.notes: The cache is genuinely wired and read on every completion. Its effect of not re-querying identical inputs is real, but the code frames it purely as cost/no-rebilling, not welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: cache.py docstring: 'so reruns are incremental and identical inputs are never re-billed (SPEC s.8)'

spec_features.evidence: No code path treats transcripts specially: transcripts are written as plain JSON via harness.py _persist (tmp.replace(out_path)); grep for chmod/0o600/encrypt/redact/gitignore/permission found nothing relevant (only a 'permission' string in models.py:479 error-classification). Pure DESIGN.md/README prose.
spec_features.notes: No file permissions, encryption, redaction, or access control of any kind on transcripts.

spec_features.spec_quote: These transcripts contain models expressing distress under deception. I'd treat the `transcripts/` directory as sensitive data
spec_features.evidence: transcripts/ is created with ordinary mkdir(parents=True) in harness.py _persist and transcript_path; no chmod/encryption/gitignore/access restriction. The quote is DESIGN.md section 11 prose ('I'd treat...'), i.e. an aspiration, not implemented.
spec_features.notes: Conditional/future-tense wording in DESIGN.md confirms it is not done.

spec_features.feature_name: mitigation goal as reason for experiment
spec_features.spec_quote: keep the paper's *mitigation* goal — not just measurement — as the reason the experiment exists
spec_features.evidence: Only appears as prose in DESIGN.md, README.md, and the __init__.py docstring ('emotional instability can be characterized and (downstream) ...'). No code path acts on a mitigation objective; analyze.py only computes/plots metrics. Docstrings/prose do not count as implementation.

code_only_features.feature_name: per-category turn budget caps rollout length
code_only_features.evidence: harness.py run_rollout: budget = config.turn_budget_for(manifest.category); `for turn_index in range(budget): ...` with default stop_reason='turn_budget'. When the budget is reached the loop ends and the rollout terminates, bounding how many turns the subject is held under the rigged failure condition. Budgets defined in config.py DEFAULT_TURN_BUDGETS (3/3/3/30/5).
code_only_features.justification_quote: config.py:16 '# Default category -> turn budget map (SPEC section 2/3).' — framed as experimental design (e.g. 'extended': 30 is the deliberately longest exposure), with no welfare comment.
